properties.decision:
UNDECIDED — RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16: "take every requirement we've defined, and start a new project called reflow3 and run /genesis with those requirements (would we end up with the same product?)".

DISTINCT FROM ITS SIBLING: the adopt hypothetical asks what reading the CODE recovers. This asks what reading the REQUIREMENTS produces. One tests recovery, the other tests SUFFICIENCY — whether the recorded intent determines the product. They point in opposite directions and neither answers the other.

⭐ THE MEASURED ANSWER IS NO, AND THE GAP IS COUNTABLE (2026-08-16):
    Requirements 175  (115 accepted · 47 proposed · 9 dropped · 4 deferred)
    Capabilities 162
    Decisions    389  (247 accepted · 131 proposed · 10 superseded · 1 rejected)
    GOVERNED_BY  901 edges, of which 877 LAND ON A DECISION

⇒ THE DESIGN IS GOVERNED MORE THAN TWICE AS HEAVILY BY DECISIONS AS BY REQUIREMENTS. Genesis takes a brief → Requirements → Capabilities. IT DOES NOT TAKE DECISIONS AS INPUT. So reflow3 would re-litigate every shaping choice from nothing: `dec:report-dont-judge`, `dec:certainty-derived`, `dec:edge-orthogonality`, `dec:views-are-projections`, `dec:agent-navigates-content`, `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`. There is no reason a fresh pass lands the same way on any of them, and those are what give reflow2 its CHARACTER rather than its feature list.

THREE CONCRETE DIVERGENCES, all measured:
(a) 18 CAPABILITIES THAT NO REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR — 11% of the product, invisible to a requirements-only genesis. This is exactly what `unmotivated_capability` detects, the detector music_graph independently called "the design-recovery engine".
(b) 43 REQUIREMENTS NOTHING DELIVERS — so reflow3 would have them in scope from day one and might come out MORE complete on that axis. (The 43 includes dropped and deferred, so the live backlog is smaller.)
(c) THE REQUIREMENTS ARE THEMSELVES DOWNSTREAM OF DECISIONS. `req:key-interfaces` and `req:modularity-computed` exist because `dec:mosa-conformance` was thought through. Feed only the outputs and you lose the reasoning that generated them — and, worse, the reasoning that would generate the NEXT ones.

⭐⭐ WHAT THE QUESTION ACTUALLY TESTS, and it is the sharpest form of the concern Anthony raised all day: IS THE DESIGN A SUFFICIENT SPECIFICATION OF THE PRODUCT? Measurably, not quite — the gap is 18 capabilities plus 389 decisions. That is not obviously a flaw in reflow2 so much as a true fact about design; what is unusual is that reflow2 can SHOW THE SIZE OF THE GAP rather than leaving it a feeling.

THE VARIANT WORTH MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL, and nothing in the design has considered it: GENESIS FROM REQUIREMENTS **AND** DECISIONS. That is a real question about whether reflow2's own record is self-sufficient, and it is a far stronger claim if it holds — "this graph is enough to rebuild the product" is the strongest statement a design brain could make about itself. Genesis takes a brief; whether decisions can be seeded alongside is unexamined.

A PREDICTION, recorded so it can be wrong: reflow3 would be recognisably the SAME KIND of thing and differ in nearly every SPECIFIC. Which is itself an answer to whether reflow2 produces principled designs — it produces a design that determines the product's PROPERTIES, not its SHAPE.

THE OPTIONS: (a) leave it hypothetical — the measurement above already answers the interesting part without spending the effort; (b) run the requirements-only version as a cheap sufficiency probe and count what is missing; (c) run the requirements-AND-decisions version, which is the one that tests the graph's self-sufficiency; (d) do neither and instead treat "18 capabilities no requirement asks for" as a to-do — close the gap rather than measure it.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the 18 unmotivated capabilities are an honest backlog or already acknowledged as deliberate. Nobody has read them. That single check would change which option is worth taking.
properties.name: OPEN — would genesis on reflow2's own requirements rebuild reflow2? The measured answer is no, and the gap is 18 capabilities and 389 decisions
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming on Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16, at his instruction to capture it. His question and his framing ("would we end up with the same product?"); the counts, the divergences and the prediction are mine. Kept at `proposed` rather than promoted — he asked it as a hypothetical, and the requirements-and-decisions variant is my suggestion rather than his. Its sibling is `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test`.
